title: Project build & dependency folders
_comment: Regenerable folders inside your CODE REPOS. The tool groups findings per project — one git repo = one row — so you can pick which repos to clean. 'scan.groups' name directories that hold a CROWD of machine-generated repos (e.g. an AI agent that keeps every session as its own git repo under ~/.gemini/antigravity/brain); every repo at or under a group root collapses into ONE aggregate row keyed by the root instead of flooding the menu with dozens of near-identical rows. Add a directory here to fold its child repos together; it is a display grouping only — each item is still deleted individually and gated by is_safe_target. 'scan.roots' are searched up to maxDepth; interior dirs named in 'prune' are skipped (this list also excludes tool/cache homes like ~/.npm, ~/.cargo, ~/.local so language caches, global npm, editor extensions and the like are never mistaken for your projects — those are covered by the dev-cache rules instead). kind:project entries only define the regenerable dir NAMES to match (and the method); they are deleted with rm. A name match only NOMINATES a directory: every one is then verified to be git-ignored (and untracked) in its own repo before it can be offered, so a tracked build/ of release scripts, a committed dist/ or a vendored Pods/ is left alone — enforced in scan_projects, not here, and a dir that no .gitignore covers is never offered however well its name matches (see docs/DESIGN.md#ignored-proof). kind:gitignore enumerates every git-ignored entry via 'git ls-files --others --ignored --directory' per repo and moves them to the Trash (recoverable — git-ignored files can include local config); .env* files are never offered for deletion regardless of rules (they hold secrets/local config nothing can regenerate — enforced in scan_projects, not here). Junk found outside any git repo is ignored. IMPORTANT: a name must NOT appear in both 'prune' and a category's 'dirs' — the find expression evaluates the prune branch first, so a pruned name can never be reported. Names matched as junk are pruned anyway (find does not descend into them), so moving a name out of 'prune' into 'dirs' costs no scan time.
